purpose: Second pass over the 19 players with unknown 2026 salary values in the pilot dataset, followed by a credentialed Daily Telegraph / SMH source pass.

top30Confidence.summary: The named roster is credible as a working NRL roster, but not fully reliable as a clean Top 30 because Wests Tigers' own tracker lists some players in both NRL Squad and NRL Development List contexts, while the NRL tracker omits Bunty Afoa from the current Wests Tigers list despite listing him as a 2026 gain/loss movement.

ambiguousNames.name: Bunty Afoa
ambiguousNames.reason: Wests Tigers tracker lists him in the NRL Development List for 2026; NRL tracker lists him as a 2026 movement to Wests Tigers but omits him from the current Wests Tigers contract table.

ambiguousNames.name: Javon Andrews
ambiguousNames.reason: Wests Tigers tracker says he arrives on a Development deal, while NRL tracker lists 2026-2028 years in the Wests Tigers section.

ambiguousNames.name: Patrick Herbert
ambiguousNames.reason: Club article says two-year NRL deal, but Wests Tigers tracker also lists him in the NRL Development List for 2026.

ambiguousNames.name: Faaletino Tavana
ambiguousNames.reason: Club article says extension through 2029, but Wests Tigers tracker also lists Tino Tavana in the NRL Development List for 2026.

salaryFindings.name: Adam Doueihi
salaryFindings.finding: Daily Telegraph/Code Sports roster-value investigation lists Adam Doueihi at $725k. Found a separate older $150k near-minimum offer, but that related to an earlier short-term contract discussion rather than the 2026-2029 extension.

salaryFindings.name: Sione Fainu
salaryFindings.finding: Daily Telegraph/Code Sports roster-value investigation lists Sione Fainu at $405k. SMH separately reports a three-year, $1.1m extension, implying about $367k average annual value for the extension years. Treat the SMH figure as 2027-2029 extension context unless a source confirms it changes 2026.

salaryFindings.name: Bunty Afoa
salaryFindings.finding: Club source confirms 2026 signing; Wests tracker lists him under NRL Development List. If supplementary/development treatment applies, use the relevant NRL list salary bucket rather than Top 30 cap.

notes: The NRL salary cap rules page supports a 2026 Top 30 minimum salary floor derived from the 2023-2027 minimum salary progression.
The NRL operations page states Supplementary List players are entitled to $80,000 p.a.; Wests Tigers uses Development List wording, so these records need category confirmation before display.
For UI, show minimum/floor-derived values as a distinct low-confidence band, not as reported salary.
